exec-gas-applies-refund.why: EIP-7778 reverted: the block counts post-refund gas, so the receipt figure and the block figure merge again (class 13)

exec-gas-no-state-subtraction.replace:
gas_used_before_refund,  # MUTATION: state term dropped
            calldata_floor,
exec-gas-no-state-subtraction.why: drop `- settled_state_gas_used`: state gas is counted in both block dimensions instead of one (class 14)

state-clamp-min.why: invert the net-state-gas clamp (max -> min): state creation stops reaching block accounting (class 14)

state-clamp-off.why: remove the max(0, ...) clamp entirely. EXPECTED TO SURVIVE: measured `state_gas_used` is never negative under the reference refund rules (10 adversarial shapes, all 0 or +97,920), so the clamp is an identity -- see tests/state_gas_clamp/README.md for the arithmetic

state-free-credit.why: make freeing state generous, the one rule change that can actually drive `state_gas_used` negative: it is the mutation the class-14 invariant is defined against (class 14)

floor-not-a-max.replace: gas_used = gas_used_after_refund  # MUTATION: the floor stops binding
floor-not-a-max.why: the calldata floor is no longer a floor on the sender-facing charge, so a refund becomes visible again (class 15)

floor-token-8.why: EIP-7976 half-reverted (16 -> 8 per floor token). EXPECTED TO SURVIVE, and the surviving side of a located cliff: at 4,096 calldata bytes the floor becomes 15,000 + 16,384*8 = 146,072, still above the refunding transaction's post-refund 141,908, so the floor keeps binding (class 15)

floor-token-7.why: the biting side of the same cliff: 15,000 + 16,384*7 = 129,688 falls below the post-refund 141,908, the floor stops binding for the refunding transaction only, and the refund becomes visible in the sender's balance (class 15)

refund-divisor-4.why: refund cap divisor 5 -> 4, the EIP-3529 lever: it moves the sender-facing figure and therefore the size of the block-versus-sender gap (class 13)
